title: Spiritual Zion
english: The law will emanate from Zion and the word of the Lord will be proclaimed from Jerusalem, and it will announce to us His way, and we will walk in it (Isaiah 2:3).

As the memory of the prophecy over them has come, the prophet indicates the time during which the power of the devil will not fall on any part of the earth or in one place and city, but rather this disease will be taken from all under heaven, and the tyranny of the unclean demons will be broken, with the worship of idols and the wicked construction having been removed from everywhere.

The vision has ended for him, and the end of the prophecy that has already arrived was, because they will be ashamed of their idols, which they wanted, and they were ashamed of their gardens, which they desired.

In the way that the Israelites were ashamed of their idols, which they had desired, they will also be ashamed of their gardens, which they had desired, and this shame is a continuous theme that we have discussed.

In the last days, that is, in the last times of the present age, the only-begotten Word of God has shone, having become from a woman, and He has presented to Himself the intelligible Judah, that is, Jerusalem, that is, the virgin Church, pure and unblemished, without stain or wrinkle, as it is written: holy and unblemished (Ephesians 5:27).
The prophet says about the Church that in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of God of Jacob will be established on the tops of the mountains.
To us, Zion, which is in Judea, is said to be situated on a mountain and built, but one would think of the Church, not sensibly, but spiritually, as being likened to a mountain.

The Church is truly high and conspicuous, and well-known to all, for it is elevated above earthly things and, as far as possible, contemplates God's glory with the eyes of the mind, boasting of lofty doctrines about Him.

In contrast, the Greek sophists, who deify creation and pay homage to the elements of the world, demonstrate their lowly mind and earthly speculations, and, claiming to be wise, they became fools, as it is written (Romans 1:22).

The Church surpasses all visible and invisible creation, and reaches the nature that is beyond all things, for it is filled with divine light, and, knowing itself and the Creator and Artisan of all things, it alone receives the power that is over all things.
And with this glory He will crown.
translator_notes: The Greek source ends mid-word with 'στεφα', which is likely part of 'στεφανωθησεται' or a similar verb form. The translation renders this as an incomplete phrase with a leading ellipsis to reflect the cut-off, avoiding any invented completion.

title: God's Rebuke of Humanity
english: Our God, who loves us, is grieved by the insatiable greed that characterizes humanity, much like horses being restrained, and those who are snared by the nooses of love of glory.

The land is filled with the presence of horses, indicating that the disease of pride has spread throughout the land, affecting not just a few individuals, but rather, as if the whole land is occupied by this passion, and evil pervades everything.

God rebukes those who have stumbled against the law and disobeyed Him, having deliberately disobeyed God, who has spoken clearly, saying, 'If you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, and you inherit it and live in it, and you say, "I will set up a ruler over myself, just like the other nations around me," then you shall set up as ruler over yourself one whom the Lord your God chooses' (Deuteronomy 17:14-15).

Furthermore, God also says about the one being set up, 'He will not multiply horses for himself, nor will he turn the people back to Egypt, so that he may not multiply horses for himself; and he will not greatly multiply silver and gold for himself' (Deuteronomy 17:16-17).

As a result, God blames humanity for making a collection of wealth and multiplying horses for themselves without limit, which is a transgression of His commandment, for He is the Lord your God, who has given them the land as an inheritance.

This reproach, as is likely, touches most of all those who have been allotted to lead, for they are the ones who should be setting an example, yet they are the ones who are disobeying God's commandment, which they were supposed to follow and uphold before others, and to rebuke those who transgress, as they were the ones who were supposed to be followed and seen as having been honored before others.
The land was filled with the abominations of the works of their hands, and they worshiped what their fingers had made.
And a man bowed down, and a human was humbled, and God will not lift them up.
God again accuses humanity of spiritual adultery, and the fact that many chose to worship false gods.

He declares that humanity has reached the limit of impiety, as if to exhaust all evil, and to contemplate the most complete apostasy from God, who knows all things, and gives signs and hints towards existence.
It seems that in some way, human nature, which has been utterly insulted, is suffering excessively.

For the God of all things honored humanity with self-sufficiency, creating humans not just with a word, like other creations, but by taking dust from the earth and making humans, according to the words of the all-wise Moses.
Humans were made in the image and likeness of God, and became a kind of ruler over the things on earth.
Humans were also honored with the spirit of life, for God breathed the breath of life into their face.

Therefore, the scripture says that humans, being in honor, did not understand, for they worshiped carved idols, and, as the prophetic word said, they bowed down to what their fingers had made (Psalm 49:20).
The scripture also says, 'Man, who is in honor, does not understand' (Psalm 49:20).
Despite this, humanity has chosen to disobey God's commandment, and has instead accumulated wealth and multiplied horses for themselves without limit.
As a result, God will not lift them up, and they will remain in their state of humiliation and bondage to their own desires.
translator_notes: The translation of certain words, such as 'νοητὴν πορνείαν', may be uncertain or open to interpretation.
The phrase 'καὶ μάλα εἰκότως ὁ φιλάρετος ἡμῶν Θεὸς' is a complex sentence that requires careful translation to convey the intended meaning.
The biblical quotation 'Ἐὰν δὲ εἰσέλθῃς εἰς τὴν γῆν... αὐτὸν' is from Deuteronomy 17:14-15.
The phrase 'Προσεκύνησαν οἷς ἐποίησαν οἱ δάκτυλοι αὐτῶν' is an allusion to Isaiah 2:8.
The text appears to be incomplete at the beginning and end, with the source chunk starting and ending mid-sentence.

title: Spiritual Nourishment
english: The spiritual nourishment that comes from God is not just about physical bread and water, but about the power of bread and the power of water. This is what we must desire to teach, for when we encounter sacred words and read the divine Scriptures, we receive the power of spiritual bread. As it is written, 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.'

The Jews, however, still cling to the physical bread and water, busy with the writings of Moses and reading the law. But since they do not understand the spiritual significance, they do not have the power of bread or the power of water. The Scripture testifies to this through Paul, who says that a veil lies on their heart when they read Moses, and that it is done away with in Christ. We, on the other hand, who have been called to sanctification through faith, have the bread that comes from heaven, which is Christ, or his body. And the power of this bread is life-giving, for it gives life to the world.

We approach the grace of holy baptism, which sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually, conforming us to Christ. This baptism also gives us a bold entrance into the kingdom of heaven, as Jesus said, 'Unless one is born of water and spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God.' The Jews, however, lack this gift, for they do not have the power of bread, which is the life-giving power in Christ, nor do they have the power of water.

As a result, unforgiven sin remains with them, and they will not enter the kingdom of heaven, having dishonored Christ who brings them in. They did not believe him when he said, 'I am the way and the door.' Christ takes away both the giant and the strong, and we must understand who these are. The giant is the one who has come to the language of spiritual power, and the strong is the one who has been humbled and overcome by the superiority in it. Each of us has been given a measure of God's grace, as the apostle Paul said, 'I want all men to be like me.'
